title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Oregon and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the winery, grape, AVA, like Willamette Valley or Dundee Hills, and vintage. Oregon's rules are strict: 90% of a named grape, 95% from a named AVA, and no use of European place names like Burgundy. Most wineries are small and family-owned; many are certified sustainable, LIVE, or biodynamic.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Willamette Pinot Noir suits salmon, especially Pacific Northwest grilled or cedar-plank salmon, duck, mushrooms, truffles, pork and roast chicken. Pinot Gris suits seafood, Dungeness crab and Asian food. Chardonnay suits halibut and creamy dishes. Serve Pinot at 14 to 16 degrees.

steps.prompt: Which regional dish is a classic with Oregon Pinot Noir?
steps.explanation: Salmon is a Pacific Northwest staple.

steps.body: Oregon truffles, found in the Willamette Valley's forests, are a local match for aged Pinot Noir.

steps.prompt: Oregon wineries may label wines with European place names like Burgundy.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Oregon's labelling rules are among America's strictest
Pinot Noir suits salmon, duck and mushrooms
